subject: Asymmetric return-path + MTU regression — uploads failing on private deployment
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@maplecloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@maplecloud.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Large-file uploads failing to private deployment (intermittent)

Hi Neha,

Since we cut the private deploy to our on-prem DC last night, a subset of our clients report failures uploading files > 2MB to the mounted endpoint behind the private link. Failures appear intermittent: most finish but ~10% of attempts end with stalled connections and heavy retransmits.

We've attached the initial ticket from our support queue (support-ticket-45321.pdf) and a short pcaps capture from one affected host. Can Redwood help triage? Happy to give you access to a packet capture host and a topology diagram if useful.

Thanks,
Ellen

Date: 2027-03-10T13:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Large-file uploads failing to private deployment (intermittent)

Quick triage notes from pcap (capture-session-20270310.pcap.gz):
- Observed MSS/MTU mismatch: upstream segment from customer edge is allowed 1500, but on the private link we have a leftover jumbo (9000) config on a transit interface. Large frames are being fragmented/blackholed mid-path.
- More critical: return TCP segments for affected flows are traversing a different egress (asymmetric return path) and hit a stateful NAT box on their side that performs SNAT with a different source IP. We see SYN->SYN/ACK succeed, but subsequent large-data segments trigger retransmits after MTU-related ICMP or silent drops.
- There are clear signs of middlebox rewriting: conntrack shows mismatched 5-tuple on return and we see RSTs or retransmit storms.

Hypothesis: combination of MTU mismatch + asymmetric return path + a SNAT rewrite on MapleCloud firewall is causing connection reassembly failures for larger payloads.

Attached sample from pcap and I noted the timestamps where retransmits spike.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@maplecloud.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Large-file uploads failing to private deployment (intermittent)

I reproduced a variant in our staging with the following notes:
- When we force traffic through a single symmetric path (pinning the return), the uploads complete reliably.
- When we restore the asymmetric route, large transfers fail in the same pattern as MapleCloud capture.

Proposed mitigations (short-term -> long-term):
1) Short-term (hotfix): enable MSS clamping on our egress to the private link to 1360 (accounts for headers), and apply an egress MTU sanity check on the private-link interface. This avoids fragmentation and large packet drops.
2) Customer action: ask MapleCloud to preserve source IPs through their SNAT or add a SNAT mapping that preserves 5-tuple symmetry for the private link routes. Alternatively, add an explicit return-path policy so return packets do not traverse the alternate egress that rewrites flows.
3) Long-term: extend our route pinning/flow-sticky option for private deployments (SRE project) so we can enforce symmetric paths for session-critical flows.

If team agrees I'll schedule the MSS clamp change as an immediate patch; it is low-risk but will require a short maintenance window on the private link.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@maplecloud.com>

Date: 2027-03-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Large-file uploads failing to private deployment (intermittent)

Thanks — that matches our suspicion. We can:
- Push a temporary route pinning rule to keep return traffic on the same egress for the MapleCloud -> Redwood CIDR pair.
- Coordinate a firewall rule change to preserve client source IPs for the private link (vendor is Titan Connect; FW list below).

Can you send a short runbook for the MSS clamp change and a proposed 15-minute maintenance window? We'll aim to do this during our low-traffic window tomorrow 2027-03-12 02:00-03:00 UTC. Also attaching our topology (topology-map-v3.png) and vendor contact for Titan Connect.

Ellen
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@maplecloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Large-file uploads failing to private deployment (intermittent)

Team — plan and next steps.

Decision: apply short-term MSS clamp and interface MTU sanity check on Redwood egress + request MapleCloud to apply SNAT-preserve rule / return-path pinning. If issues persist, escalate to SRE for a code-level sticky-flow rollout.

Runbook (short):
- Window: 2027-03-12 02:00-02:30 UTC (customer approved).
- Steps on Redwood egress (performed by infra team):
  1) Verify current MTU on private-link interface and backup config.
  2) Apply MSS clamping policy on egress to 1360 for TCP sessions toward MapleCloud CIDRs.
  3) Restart flow-engine process (non-disruptive) and monitor conntrack and retransmit counters for 15 minutes post-change.
- Customer actions (MapleCloud):
  1) Temporarily pin return path for Redwood CIDRs (routing rule) OR
  2) Update firewall SNAT policy to preserve original source or create symmetric SNAT mapping.

Attachments included: capture-session-20270310.pcap.gz, topology-map-v3.png.

Marissa will coordinate the maintenance window calendar invite with MapleCloud. Vanessa/Karthik — pls own the infra change and post a short post-change note with traffic metrics. If we still see failures after both sides change, I'll escalate to SRE to push the sticky-flow hotfix (Jira-RED-45321).

Thanks everyone — will follow up with the invite.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
